name: Media, Arts and Entertainment
description: An interpretive blueprint for music, hip-hop, media, narratives, audiences, creative work, and cultural impact.

guidance: Define the works, creators, genres or forms, production and circulation context, audience, period, and interpretive lens.
Separate formal observation, source statement, interpretation, reception evidence, commercial evidence, and broader cultural claim.
Analyze form and technique together with themes, voice, representation, context, audience, circulation, and influence.
Ground interpretation in specific works, passages, scenes, sonic or visual features, patterns, or reception evidence.
Represent competing readings and avoid treating one critic, fan group, market signal, or platform metric as universal reception.
Prefer thematic grids, evidence trails, and influence pathways; chart only meaningful timelines, distributions, or comparable audience evidence.
Respect source wording and attribution while keeping quotations brief and distinguishing influence from simple chronology.

sections.title: Creative Context and Interpretive Answer
sections.purpose: Identify the creative subject and context, then answer the objective with a grounded interpretive thesis.

blocks.title: Works, Context and Evidence Profile
instructions: Identify works, creators, forms or genres, period, production or release context, audience evidence, and material coverage gaps.

blocks.title: Interpretive Thesis
instructions: Answer the objective with a clear thesis connecting form, theme, context, and significance using the strongest concrete evidence.
Distinguish interpretation from documented creator intent and audience reception.

blocks.title: Creative and Cultural Findings
instructions: Present distinct findings about form, technique, theme, voice, representation, context, audience, circulation, tension, or influence.

sections.title: Form, Technique and Meaning
sections.purpose: Explain how specific creative choices produce, complicate, or contest meaning.

blocks.title: Formal and Thematic Analysis
instructions: Analyze specific compositional, sonic, visual, narrative, performance, genre, language, or editing choices and connect them to themes.
Avoid broad thematic claims without a concrete feature, work, passage, or pattern.

blocks.title: From Form to Cultural Meaning
instructions: Map one supported chain from creative choice through audience cue or circulation context to interpretation or cultural effect; mark contested links.

sections.title: Context, Audience and Reception
sections.purpose: Place the creative work in historical, social, industrial, and audience contexts while preserving multiple readings.

blocks.title: Context and Reception Analysis
instructions: Analyze relevant historical, social, technological, industrial, platform, market, and audience contexts with competing interpretations.
Do not treat sales, streams, awards, or one response as complete cultural impact.

blocks.title: Comparable Audience or Circulation Evidence

chart_slot.intent: Support one claim with comparable audience, circulation, timeline, catalog, or reception evidence.

fallback.message: No comparable quantitative audience or circulation evidence is available.

instructions: Preserve platform, territory, period, denominator, catalog scope, and metric definition; do not convert popularity into quality or universal reception.

sections.title: Works, Passages and Evidence
sections.purpose: Make the interpretive basis auditable and identify productive avenues for further creative or cultural inquiry.

blocks.title: Creative Evidence Trail
instructions: Tie findings to works, scenes, passages, formal details, performances, interviews, reviews, audience records, or source locations; paraphrase by default.

blocks.title: Further Interpretive Questions
instructions: Offer questions or comparative avenues that follow from genuine tensions or gaps; do not prescribe a single authoritative reading.

sections.title: Interpretive Limits and Missing Perspectives
sections.purpose: State which absent works, contexts, voices, audience evidence, or methodological choices constrain the interpretation.

blocks.title: Limitations and Counter-Readings
instructions: Identify missing works, versions, production context, creator testimony, audience groups, territories, reception sources, historical context, or plausible counter-readings only when material.
